characterList.description: A young Asian woman with long black hair, wearing a pink sweater and a white shirt. She sits on the left side of the screen.
characterList.name: Wei-Lun Hsu

characterList.description: An older Caucasian man with white hair and glasses, wearing a blue shirt. He sits on the right side of the screen.
characterList.name: Keith Dunker

content_metadata.description: Analyzing a video presentation on the research of intrinsically disordered proteins led by Wei-Lun Hsu and Keith Dunker, the video explores protein binding diversity, research strategies, findings, and their implications.

qAndA.question: What is the sequence identity threshold used to select binding partners in the study?
How many protein 'hubs' were identified in the study?

qAndA.answer: Class 1 proteins exhibit similar folds with different side-chain orientations, while Class 2 proteins have completely distinct folds. (1:45 - 2:14)
qAndA.question: What distinguishes Class 1 proteins from Class 2?
Which specific protein segment is the focus of the second class of 'hubs'?
What factors besides conformational diversity might influence partner selection by intrinsically disordered proteins?

Video highlight from authors Keith Dunker and Wei-Lun Hsu on their recently published Protein Science paper entitled, "Exploring the binding diversity of intrinsically disordered proteins involved in one-to-many binding."
Read the paper online:
http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/pro.2207/abstract
